key_insight: KANs can predict airfoil surface pressure well and interpolate across Mach number and angle of attack, but they do not clearly outperform a well-tuned MLP and are generally below a GNN on accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a lower-complexity, faster-training alternative that may be attractive when interpretability and speed matter, but performance gains are not guaranteed.
method: Compared Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) against multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and graph neural networks (GNNs).
Target task: surface pressure coefficient prediction on subsonic and transonic airfoils.
Evaluated interpolation across Mach numbers and angles of attack.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs achieve good pressure-distribution predictions, with performance comparable but marginally inferior to a suitably trained MLP, while the best accuracy comes from a GNN at the cost of longer training.
watch_item: KAN performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and can suffer from training instabilities.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
